newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NATO military hopes for command deal for summit.
newsitem.headline: NATO military hopes for command deal for summit.

text.p: The head of NATO's military chiefs said on Wednesday he was confident that the alliance would agree on a new command structure in time for a July summit intended to launch its eastern European expansion project.

"We hope we will be in a position prior to the summit to propose to the NATO council a fully agreed command structure for NATO," Military Committee chairman Klaus Naumann told a news conference at the end of a two-day meeting.
The chiefs of staff failed during their meeting to agree the share-out of posts and commands within a streamlined alliance adapted to take account of the realities of the post-Cold War world.
Naumann said the only sticking point was how to define the number of regional commands in the 16-nation alliance's south.
"We need to define the number of regional commands in the south. That is the only point on which we have not agreement," he said.
The proposals aim to reduce NATO's Cold War defence posture from four command levels to three.

In addition, a new streamlined network of sub-regional commands, each capable of limited out-of-area operations, would report to two rather than three regional commands -- one in the north, one in the south.
The reforms are considered essential if the alliance is to be able to take on more Bosnia-style operations, cope with the influx of new members from former communist Europe and make savings.
Neumann said the current package would move the alliance to as low as 20 headquarters at three levels from 65 headquarters at four command levels.
In the south, Greece, Turkey, Italy, Spain and Portugal all want a command on their territory, while the military say only two are needed, NATO officials have said.
The final decision lies with NATO Defence Ministers, Naumann stressed.
